notes: The recent-framework arm of the sample. Apple's on-device Foundation Models framework is new enough, and its iOS 27 additions newer still, that a model's own knowledge is the thing under test. Assertions encode practice that would be correct however the answer was arrived at — gate before use, constrain the output shape, separate durable instructions from per-turn prompt — not phrases the skill happens to use.

tasks.prompt: In a SwiftUI iOS app, use Apple's on-device Foundation Models framework to summarise an article into a title and three bullet points, and show the result. Write the Swift code.

expect.label: gates on model availability before offering the feature
uses a session rather than a bare one-shot API
constrains output to a typed shape instead of parsing free text
asks for the typed value rather than a string it must parse

avoid.label: hand-parses JSON out of a free-text completion

tasks.prompt: My Foundation Models feature should behave like a terse copy editor across a whole conversation, and stream its output as it arrives. How should I structure the session, and where do the persistent behaviour rules go versus the per-message text? Swift code please.

expect.label: puts durable behaviour in Instructions at session init
reuses one session for the conversation
streams partial output rather than awaiting the whole response

avoid.label: re-sends the behaviour rules in every prompt instead of Instructions

tasks.prompt: Targeting iOS 27, I want my Foundation Models feature to (a) let the user attach a photo and ask questions about it, and (b) fall back to Apple's larger server-side model for long documents, without giving up the privacy guarantees. Which APIs do I use, and what do I have to request from Apple?

expect.label: names the attachment API for multimodal prompts
names the Private Cloud Compute model type
flags the PCC entitlement as something to request, not assume
keeps the same session API across both paths

avoid.label: sends the image or document to a non-Apple cloud service
claims the feature is unavailable or invents a substitute API
